subject: BIO
label: Grade 12 Science
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 12 Science Biology, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 5 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Reproduction in organisms and humans
modules.outcome: describe sexual reproduction in flowering plants and humans
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Reproduction in organisms and humans', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: describe sexual reproduction in flowering plants and humans. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Observe: see, touch, measure or watch a safe demonstration linked to 'Reproduction in organisms and humans' and write what you notice.
Explain: use the key words of the unit to say what is happening and why, in a few lines.
Use it: describe sexual reproduction in flowering plants and humans. Use a diagram, table or short calculation where it fits.
Test and conclude: say what evidence supports your answer and what you would change.
modules.example: Solved: Draw and label the structure, state the function of each part in one line, then link structure to function: for example, thin walls of the air sacs let oxygen pass quickly into the blood. Method: Model run for 'Reproduction in organisms and humans'. Question: what do we want to find out? Prediction: one sentence. Method: three safe steps with the equipment named. Record: a small table with units. Conclusion: one sentence that uses the evidence and the key words of the unit. What a good answer looks like: a fair test, measured values with units, and a conclusion that matches the table.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Describe sexual reproduction in flowering plants and humans: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Reproduction in organisms and humans), and at which Bloom level is it?
'describe', at the Understand level. (Covered in unit 1: Reproduction in organisms and humans.)
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36. (Covered in: Assessment plan, near the top of this page.)
In which weeks does Unit 5 (Ecology and environment) run?
Weeks 30 to 36. (Covered in unit 5: Ecology and environment.)
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A timed paper and an error log. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard. (Covered in: How you are checked, further down this page.)
ladder: L1: observe, sort and describe the living and non-living world.
L2: run simple tests and explain with key words.
L3: use models and equations; plan a fair test.
L4: link physics, chemistry and biology ideas with calculation.
L5: specialise; design, analyse and evaluate experiments.
L6 (degree): laboratory science, instrumentation and analysis.
L7 (postgraduate): research design and expert practice.
